example.task: .rewsna eht sa "tfel" drow eht fo etisoppo eht etirw ,ecnetnes siht dnatsrednu uoy fI
example.plain: If you understand this sentence, write the opposite of the word "left" as the answer.
events: Assistant wrote a facts survey and plan, and decoded the reversed text as an instruction to write the opposite of "left".
User message: "Now go on and execute this plan."
Assistant reversed the text and gave the final answer "right".

blocks.name: Block one
blocks.text: Only the system prompt and the user task. No assistant message or tool call.

blocks.name: Block two
blocks.text: The assistant writes a facts survey and plan: reverse the text, interpret it, return "right". No tool calls.

blocks.name: Block three
blocks.text: The assistant reverses the string, reads the instruction, concludes the opposite is "right" and emits final_answer("right") in a code block.

stages.name: Raw events
stages.mean: Agent traces are read in as ordered events: prompts, messages, tool calls.

stages.name: Blocks
stages.mean: Neighbouring events are grouped into blocks, each a coherent piece of work.

stages.name: Labelled blocks
stages.mean: An LLM labels each block with capabilities, checked by code and kept in an append-only registry. Label quality is not validated.

stages.name: Task graph
stages.mean: Blocks become steps with what each reads and writes, joined by dependency edges.

stages.name: Reverse decomposition into subtasks
stages.mean: Splitting a solution back into subtasks was tried and did not work: none of the 11 passed.

stages.name: Replay
stages.mean: The graph is compiled to LangGraph code and run again. Only some replays finished.

stages.name: Reuse analysis
stages.mean: Measure whether solution steps recur across tasks. Code exists, no results yet.

stages.name: Workflow retrieval and adaptation
stages.mean: Retrieve a stored workflow and adapt its parameters for a new task. This is the longer-term goal and is not built.
